The PR description says one ci.yml step per test file, which the diff satisfies structurally, but a job-level separation is the only way to give each test file its own green/red signal in the GitHub Actions summary.
- requirement: "The judge's `close` choice for `intervention-cap` is a single `[claude-intervention] descope ES-<n>` commit on the blocked PR's own branch; for other stops it is a new revert PR from `claude/implement-plan-<slug>-descope-<n>`" (PR description, restated in the implement-plan-clause plan and agents.md)
  expected_change_site: `.claude/commands/escalation-judge.md` step 8 descope branch (line 53) and the descope bullet in `implement-plan-claude.md` "Escalations" (line 333)
  confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: implement-plan-claude.md line 333 says: "For `intervention-cap` (the stop the `Escalation:` line names), remove the failing part from the blocked PR's own branch in one `[claude-intervention] descope ES-<n>` commit" — so the rule is documented. The judge command step 8 budget/descope branch (line 53) sets the wait and adds the line to the resume block, but does not tell the next stage (the `descope ES-<n>` stage) how to decide which form of the descope to apply. The next stage reads the `Escalation:` line and the log's `Last note` to find the stop id; it must additionally recover the blocked PR (and the original intervention history) to know whether the descope is a single commit on the blocked PR's branch or a new revert PR. The judge could record the stop id and the form choice in the resume block itself ("descope ES-N (intervention-cap) on PR #X" vs. "descope ES-N (conformance-cap) revert PR"), so the next stage does not have to re-derive it from the log.

- .claude/commands/escalation-judge.md:54 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: step 8 instructs the judge to close the source issue in issue mode via `mcp__github__issue_write` `state: closed, state_reason: not_planned`, then later in the same paragraph states "Never delete a branch and never close anything the chain did not open." The source issue is opened by the issue creation flow (or by `/implement-issue-claude` step 1), not by the project's `mcp__github__create_pull_request` chain that the `get_me` author check later restricts to, so a literal reading of the prohibition refuses the source-issue close.
  WHY: the contradiction is text the model reads, not a runtime check; a judge that resolves the contradiction by skipping the source-issue close diverges from the operator-approved contract, while a judge that closes it can hit the prohibition in its Never list and stop.
- .claude/scripts/escalation_ledger.py:249-281 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: the docstring says exit 2 fires "when the log cannot be read or an `## Escalations` line is malformed (a line that starts `- ` but does not match the format, a date that is not a real calendar date, or a repeated `ES-<n>` id)". The implementation rejects any non-blank, non-indented line in the `## Escalations` section that does not match `ENTRY_RE` (lines 262-265), so a stray line that does not start with `- ` (e.g., a blank-line edit gone wrong, or a maintainer pasting a status note inline) also triggers exit 2.
  WHY: documentation-only; the implementation is correct and `test_malformed_log_line_exits_2` already covers the broader rejection. A future maintainer patching the docstring without re-reading the loop can introduce the narrower behaviour the prose promises.
- .claude/commands/escalation-judge.md: step 5 record path and step 1 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: the close path says "A close that still fails does not stop the others: go on with the rest, and list each failed close with its error in the report so a human can finish it." Combined with the mcp__github__get_me fail-closed rule earlier in the same step (a single failed get_me read closes no PR and lists them all), the judge can end with `Status: CLOSED (not planned, ES-<n>)` set in the log but every PR the log lists still open, with only the report and one push notification to recover the state.
  WHY: the `get_me` fail-closed path lists "all of them after a failed read", while a partial close-failure path lists "each failed close with its error in the report". Two counters, two lists, and the push notification suffixes merge both under the same `; <k> PRs left open for a human, see the report` count. A judge that confuses the two paths can report zero PRs left open while the log's PR list still names open ones, leaving the operator without a clean signal.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:2254-2278 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: the §28.C paragraph was rewritten so the new text says the chain "sends no `PushNotification`, and hands its project checker the escalation wait" while leaving the prior sentence "delivered on the source issue: one comment naming the blocker, the options, and the recommended one, the `ai:claude-blocked` label, and one `PushNotification`. A human answers there and comments `/reclarify` to resume" still readable as an alternative instruction.
  WHY: a session reading the §28.C paragraph in order may apply the human-ask instructions (push notification, /reclarify resume) instead of the new escalation-wait hand-off.
- .claude/scripts/escalation_ledger.py:218-223, 367-393 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: the scratchpad-relative path check uses `resolved.relative_to(resolved_root).parts[2] != SCRATCHPAD_DIR_NAME`. `parts[2]` is the third path component, not necessarily the scratchpad directory; a project whose name contains "scratchpad" still places the scratchpad at parts[2] only when both project and session segments are single segments and the scratchpad is the third entry. `test_another_sessions_scratchpad_is_accepted` covers the depth-5 happy case, and `test_file_arguments_outside_the_scratchpad_are_refused_unread` covers the refused cases, but the script accepts a path shaped like `<root>/scratchpad/x/scratchpad/y.json` whose parts are `(scratchpad, x, scratchpad, y.json)` because parts[2] equals `scratchpad`. Inside a permissive attack surface, the check grants read access to that file.
  WHY: real-world risk is low (the system has to lay down that exact directory tree on a non-scratchpad name), and the test suite already covers the realistic threats. The check works for the documented scratchpad layout; the edge case requires deliberate path shaping, which the judge never sees in practice.
